title: 3Sum
description:
Find every distinct combination of three values from nums that adds to zero. Each combination must use three different array positions. Return no repeated triplets, even when a value appears many times in the input.

Sort each triplet in ascending order, then sort the entire list of triplets lexicographically in ascending order. Sorting the input first lets you hold one value fixed and narrow the remaining pair with two pointers; the challenge is skipping duplicates without discarding valid combinations.

Example 1:

Input: nums = [-1,0,1,2,-1,-4]
Output: [[-1,-1,2],[-1,0,1]]

Example 2:

Input: nums = [0,0,0,0]
Output: [[0,0,0]]

Example 3:

Input: nums = [-2,1,1]
Output: [[-2,1,1]]

Constraints:

  • 0 <= nums.length <= 3,000
  • -100,000 <= nums[i] <= 100,000
  • Return an empty list if fewer than three positions exist or no triplet works.

exampleTestCases.explanation: Two value combinations sum to zero; duplicate -1 positions do not create extra triplets.
Four zeros still yield just one distinct triplet.
The two ones occupy different positions.
